---

# 1. Configuración e Imports

```{r imports}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(car)        # vif, durbinWatsonTest
  library(MASS)       # rlm — soporte robusto
  library(lmtest)     # bptest — Breusch-Pagan
  library(patchwork)  # composición de gráficos
})
```

---

# 2. Carga y Preparación de Datos

```{r load-data}
# Dataset: data/flood/train.csv
# Variable dependiente : flood_prob (FloodProbability)
# Predictores          : monsoon_intensity, topography_drainage, river_management,
#                        deforestation, urbanization, wetland_loss,
#                        deteriorating_infra, political_factors

df_raw <- read_csv("data/flood/train.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

df <- df_raw %>%
  rename(
    flood_prob          = FloodProbability,
    monsoon_intensity   = MonsoonIntensity,
    topography_drainage = TopographyDrainage,
    river_management    = RiverManagement,
    deforestation       = Deforestation,
    urbanization        = Urbanization,
    wetland_loss        = WetlandLoss,
    deteriorating_infra = DeterioratingInfrastructure,
    political_factors   = PoliticalFactors
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    flood_prob, monsoon_intensity, topography_drainage, river_management,
    deforestation, urbanization, wetland_loss, deteriorating_infra,
    political_factors
  ) %>%
  drop_na()

stopifnot(nrow(df) > 100)
glimpse(df)
```

```{r fit-model, include=FALSE}
modelo <- lm(
  flood_prob ~ monsoon_intensity + topography_drainage + river_management +
               deforestation + urbanization + wetland_loss +
               deteriorating_infra + political_factors,
  data = df
)
```

---

# 3. Correlograma y VIF

```{r plot-multicolinealidad, fig.width=13, fig.height=6}
# ── Correlograma ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
num_vars <- df %>%
  dplyr::select(
    flood_prob, monsoon_intensity, topography_drainage, river_management,
    deforestation, urbanization, wetland_loss, deteriorating_infra,
    political_factors
  )

cor_mat <- cor(num_vars, use = "complete.obs")
var_ord <- colnames(cor_mat)

cor_long <- as.data.frame(cor_mat) %>%
  rownames_to_column("var1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-var1, names_to = "var2", values_to = "corr") %>%
  mutate(
    var1 = factor(var1, levels = var_ord),
    var2 = factor(var2, levels = rev(var_ord))
  )

p_corr <- ggplot(cor_long, aes(x = var1, y = var2, fill = corr)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", corr)), size = 2.5, colour = "grey10") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#d6604d",
    midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "r"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Mapa de Calor de Correlación",
    subtitle = "Predictores numéricos — FloodProbability como referencia",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1),
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 10),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

# ── VIF ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
vif_raw <- vif(modelo)

if (is.matrix(vif_raw)) {
  # car devuelve GVIF | Df | GVIF^(1/(2*Df)) para variables categóricas
  vif_df <- data.frame(
    variable = rownames(vif_raw),
    VIF      = vif_raw[, 3]^2   # (GVIF^(1/(2*Df)))^2 → comparable a VIF clásico
  )
} else {
  vif_df <- data.frame(variable = names(vif_raw), VIF = as.numeric(vif_raw))
}

p_vif <- ggplot(vif_df, aes(x = reorder(variable, VIF), y = VIF, fill = VIF)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE, width = 0.65) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 5,  linetype = "dashed", colour = "#f4a582", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10, linetype = "dotted", colour = "#d6604d", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(VIF, 2)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#74add1", high = "#d73027") +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(0, max(vif_df$VIF) * 1.25)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Factor de Inflación de la Varianza (VIF)",
    subtitle = "Umbral moderado = 5  |  Umbral crítico = 10",
    x = NULL, y = "VIF"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 10)
  )

p_corr | p_vif
```

---

# 4. Residuos Parciales (Linealidad)

```{r plot-residuos-parciales, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
numeric_preds <- c(
  "monsoon_intensity", "topography_drainage", "river_management",
  "deforestation", "urbanization", "wetland_loss",
  "deteriorating_infra", "political_factors"
)

# LOESS es O(n²): con ~1.1 M filas es inviable sobre el dataset completo.
# Un subconjunto aleatorio de 5 000 obs. es suficiente para diagnóstico visual.
set.seed(42)
n_plot   <- 5000L
idx_plot <- sample.int(nrow(df), min(n_plot, nrow(df)))
df_plot  <- df[idx_plot, ]
res_plot <- residuals(modelo)[idx_plot]

partial_plots <- map(numeric_preds, function(var) {
  beta_j    <- coef(modelo)[var]
  partial_r <- res_plot + beta_j * df_plot[[var]]
  ggplot(data.frame(x = df_plot[[var]], y = partial_r), aes(x = x, y = y)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.10, colour = "#4393c3", size = 0.6) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, colour = "#d6604d",
                fill = "#f4a582", linewidth = 1, span = 0.6,
                method.args = list(degree = 1), n = 150) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "#252525",
                linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7) +
    labs(title = var, x = var, y = "Residuo parcial") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10))
})

wrap_plots(partial_plots, ncol = 4) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Gráficos de Residuos Parciales — Diagnóstico de Linealidad",
    subtitle = "Línea roja = LOESS  |  Línea negra discontinua = relación lineal simple",
    theme    = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 11)
    )
  )
```

---

# 5. Residuos vs. Ajustados (Homocedasticidad)

```{r plot-homocedasticidad, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
# Subsample (1.1 M filas + LOESS → inviable); idx_plot definido en sección 4
hom_df <- data.frame(
  fitted  = fitted(modelo)[idx_plot],
  studres = rstudent(modelo)[idx_plot]
)

ggplot(hom_df, aes(x = fitted, y = studres)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.18, colour = "#4393c3", size = 0.9) +
  geom_hline(yintercept =  0, colour = "#252525", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept =  2, colour = "#d6604d", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -2, colour = "#d6604d", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, colour = "#b2182b",
              fill = "#f4a582", linewidth = 1.1, alpha = 0.3, span = 0.6,
              method.args = list(degree = 1), n = 150) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title    = "Residuos Estudentizados vs. Valores Ajustados",
    subtitle = "Diagnóstico de homocedasticidad  |  Umbrales de outlier: ±2",
    x = "Valores Ajustados",
    y = "Residuos Estudentizados"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 11)
  )
```

---

# 6. Q-Q Plot Avanzado (Normalidad)

```{r plot-qqplot, fig.width=8, fig.height=7}
# Subsample para Q-Q visual; idx_plot definido en sección 4
std_res <- sort(rstudent(modelo)[idx_plot])
n       <- length(std_res)
probs   <- ppoints(n)

qq_df <- data.frame(
  theoretical = qnorm(probs),
  sample      = std_res
)

# Bandas de confianza puntual al 95% (método de la envolvente normal)
se_band        <- (1 / dnorm(qq_df$theoretical)) * sqrt(probs * (1 - probs) / n)
qq_df$upper_95 <- qq_df$theoretical + 1.96 * se_band
qq_df$lower_95 <- qq_df$theoretical - 1.96 * se_band

ggplot(qq_df, aes(x = theoretical, y = sample)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower_95, ymax = upper_95),
              fill = "#92c5de", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0,
              colour = "#d6604d", linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.22, colour = "#2166ac", size = 1.1) +
  labs(
    title    = "Q-Q Plot Avanzado de Residuos Estudentizados",
    subtitle = "Banda de confianza al 95%  |  Desviaciones en las colas indican no-normalidad",
    x = "Cuantiles Teóricos (Distribución Normal)",
    y = "Cuantiles Observados (Residuos Estudentizados)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 11)
  )
```

# 7. Gráfico de Influencia (Outliers y Apalancamiento)

```{r plot-influencia, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
n_obs  <- nrow(df)
p_pred <- length(coef(modelo)) - 1   # número de coeficientes excluido el intercepto

lev_thresh <- 2 * (p_pred + 1) / n_obs  # umbral de apalancamiento estándar
out_thresh <- 2                           # umbral de residuo estudentizado

# Calcular diagnósticos sobre el dataset completo (fórmulas analíticas, rápidas)
inf_full <- data.frame(
  hat     = hatvalues(modelo),
  studres = rstudent(modelo),
  cooks   = cooks.distance(modelo)
) %>%
  mutate(
    categoria = case_when(
      hat > lev_thresh & abs(studres) > out_thresh ~ "Alto apalancamiento + Outlier",
      hat > lev_thresh                             ~ "Alto apalancamiento",
      abs(studres) > out_thresh                    ~ "Outlier",
      TRUE                                         ~ "Normal"
    ),
    categoria = factor(categoria, levels = c(
      "Normal", "Alto apalancamiento", "Outlier",
      "Alto apalancamiento + Outlier"
    ))
  )

# Conservar TODOS los puntos notables; subsamplear los normales para el gráfico
set.seed(42)
idx_normal <- which(inf_full$categoria == "Normal")
idx_keep   <- sample(idx_normal, min(4000L, length(idx_normal)))
inf_df     <- rbind(inf_full[inf_full$categoria != "Normal", ],
                    inf_full[idx_keep, ])

colour_map <- c(
  "Normal"                        = "#bbbbbb",
  "Alto apalancamiento"           = "#4393c3",
  "Outlier"                       = "#f4a582",
  "Alto apalancamiento + Outlier" = "#d6604d"
)

ggplot(inf_df, aes(x = hat, y = studres,
                   size = cooks, colour = categoria)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = lev_thresh, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "#4393c3", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept =  out_thresh, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "#d6604d", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -out_thresh, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "#d6604d", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#252525", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.45) +
  scale_size_continuous(
    name   = "Dist. de Cook",
    range  = c(0.4, 9),
    breaks = c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05)
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(name = "Clasificación", values = colour_map) +
  labs(
    title    = "Diagnóstico de Influencia: Apalancamiento vs. Residuos",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Umbral leverage = %.4f  |  Umbral |residuo| = %.0f  |  Área del punto ∝ Distancia de Cook",
      lev_thresh, out_thresh
    ),
    x = "Hat Values (Apalancamiento)",
    y = "Residuos Estudentizados"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 10),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

---

# 8. Tests Estadísticos Formales

```{r tests-formales}
cat("══════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("  TESTS FORMALES DE SUPUESTOS DE REGRESIÓN\n")
cat("══════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

# ── 1. Normalidad: Shapiro-Wilk (muestra de hasta 5000 obs.) ──────────────────
set.seed(42)
res_vec    <- residuals(modelo)
n_sw       <- min(length(res_vec), 5000)
sw_muestra <- sample(res_vec, n_sw)
sw_test    <- shapiro.test(sw_muestra)

cat(sprintf(
  "1. Shapiro-Wilk (n = %d)\n   W = %.5f  |  p-valor = %.4e\n   %s\n\n",
  n_sw, sw_test$statistic, sw_test$p.value,
  ifelse(sw_test$p.value < 0.05,
         "→ Se rechaza H0: residuos NO siguen distribución normal (p < 0.05)",
         "→ No se rechaza H0: residuos consistentes con normalidad (p ≥ 0.05)")
))

# ── 2. Homocedasticidad: Breusch-Pagan ────────────────────────────────────────
bp_test <- bptest(modelo)

cat(sprintf(
  "2. Breusch-Pagan\n   BP = %.4f  |  df = %d  |  p-valor = %.4e\n   %s\n\n",
  bp_test$statistic, bp_test$parameter, bp_test$p.value,
  ifelse(bp_test$p.value < 0.05,
         "→ Se rechaza H0: evidencia de heterocedasticidad (p < 0.05)",
         "→ No se rechaza H0: varianza constante en los residuos (p ≥ 0.05)")
))

# ── 3. Autocorrelación: Durbin-Watson ─────────────────────────────────────────
# simulate = FALSE: aproximación normal en lugar de Monte Carlo (1000 perms × 1.1M obs)
dw_test <- durbinWatsonTest(modelo, simulate = FALSE)

cat(sprintf(
  "3. Durbin-Watson\n   DW = %.4f  |  p-valor = %.4f\n   %s\n\n",
  dw_test$dw, dw_test$p,
  ifelse(dw_test$p < 0.05,
         "→ Se rechaza H0: indicios de autocorrelación en los residuos (p < 0.05)",
         "→ No se rechaza H0: no se detecta autocorrelación significativa (p ≥ 0.05)")
))

# ── 4. Multicolinealidad: VIF (resumen tabular) ────────────────────────────────
cat("4. Factor de Inflación de la Varianza (VIF)\n")
print(vif_df)
cat(sprintf(
  "\n   Máximo VIF = %.2f  |  %s\n",
  max(vif_df$VIF),
  ifelse(max(vif_df$VIF) > 10,
         "→ Multicolinealidad severa detectada (VIF > 10)",
         ifelse(max(vif_df$VIF) > 5,
                "→ Multicolinealidad moderada (5 < VIF ≤ 10)",
                "→ Sin evidencia de multicolinealidad (VIF ≤ 5)"))
))
cat("\n══════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
```
